decision: Durable complete tool material spool followed by bounded immutable chunk events in the existing outbox and reportEvents transaction; separate authorized descriptor/chunk reads. Existing 2MiB/50 event envelope stays unchanged.

alternatives.reasonRejected: Does not preserve the missing tail, exceeds recovery-file constraints, loses original bytes before persistence and still permits final/order gaps.
Unnecessary second lifetime/auth/cleanup authority for this tool-activity slice.

interface.hostPort: HarnessContext.activityBodies?: { publish(input: {activity: NativeActivityData, completeBody: Uint8Array, representation: "sdk-public-material-utf8-v1"}): Promise<void> }. Host-owned port; await means all immutable body events acknowledged, not tool success. Absent port retains explicit legacy prefix-only behavior.
interface.outbox: EventOutbox.emitActivityBody(input): serialize through the existing event tail/barrier; durable complete raw bytes and frozen event IDs/sequences before first network chunk. replayPending also consumes this fixed spool using original ownership/IDs, never reruns adapter or changes ownerVersion.
interface.wire: One new native-activity-body discriminant with a finite start/chunk/seal action schema. Existing native-activity prefix event remains unchanged. Start binds activityId/attempt/session/source identity and full bytes/digest; chunk carries index/offset/base64 bytes/sha256; seal verifies declared count, total bytes and original digest.
interface.ingestion: saveNativeActivityBody(client, task, attempt, event), assertNativeActivityBodiesFinalizable(client,attemptId). Called by existing applyEvent/reportEvents while original locks/transaction/auth remain authoritative. Final guard also covers active-steering applyEvent path.
interface.reader: GET /api/tasks/:taskId/native-activities/:activityId/body => lightweight descriptor; GET same /body/chunks?afterIndex&limit => explicit bounded bytes and stable body identity. Existing owner/browser-session route authentication; runner-role read refused. Public thin client methods supplied by Lead. No generic details endpoint for large content.
interface.identity: activityId remains SHA256(session/sourceMessage/block/kind); body ID is scoped to that immutable activity and attempt. Descriptor includes protocol, representation, full digest/declaredBytes/chunkBytes/received counts/status. Cursor is tied to body ID and index, not current task activity cursor.
interface.status: receiving | complete | interrupted; body completeness independent of tool phase/success. Absent new storage => legacy/not-recorded, never infer a recoverable tail. Pending bytes after lease/attempt ends remain incomplete; no new tail accepted once terminal.
interface.representationLimit: Preserve bytes of the provider-public material available from SDK, with explicit fixed JSON/UTF8 representation. SDK-decoded objects do not prove original network JSON whitespace/key formatting. No hidden/redacted thinking payload, auth or entire SDK frame is spooled.

candidateLimits.backpressure: One material transfer in flight per attempt; next provider material/final awaits durable completion. Bound full frame material count before accepting; upstream SDK frame allocation is outside this spool memory claim. Per-attempt retention is finite, with host worst-case multiplication by registered capacity reported rather than claiming free space reservation.

durabilityAndRecovery: Prevalidate body/aggregate/count limits; write owner-private regular file plus manifest using exclusive staging, hash/length checks, fsync file and parent, atomic publish. No symlink/arbitrary input path. Freeze event envelopes before sending; no giant pending-events JSON.

Reuse original transport pending batch and acknowledgement checks. A spool replays the same frozen batches; duplicate center events do not count twice. Lost ACK, partial write or unknown lease/fence keeps source and intent; no fresh IDs, alternate attempt or automatic model retry.

Startup recovery preserves existing current authority checks. Replay only existing frozen events; stale/completed new-tail append is refused and retained incomplete. A crash before final does not synthesize assistant-final/completed.

Final and successful completed require all announced materials sealed. Failed/cancelled ended attempt can expose interrupted material. New body events cannot follow a canonical final. Durable body seal is content-integrity evidence, not semantic/tool success.

Ordinary native activity observations remain immutable; the material/chunk tables append separate evidence. Completed manifest is immutable. Any chunk/source/digest conflict aborts the full transaction. Seal verifies the full bounded body once; no prefix aggregation on every chunk.

Body buffers never enter task snapshot/SSE: existing activity light refs stay. Explicit descriptor/chunk reader reveals body only after expansion. Existing legacy detail prefix remains readable; its historical omitted tail is unrecoverable.
